# How Much Does WhatsApp Business API Cost in Malaysia? (2026 Pricing)

WhatsApp Business API in Malaysia costs **RM0.0564 per utility message and RM0.3467 per marketing message** directly from Meta, with local BSP (Business Solution Provider) platforms adding RM299–RM999 a month on top. Combine typical messaging volume with a platform plan and most Malaysian SMEs end up paying **RM600–RM1,500 a month total**.

If you've searched "WhatsApp Business API pricing Malaysia" and come away more confused than when you started, that's normal — Meta changed the entire pricing model in July 2025, and most articles still describe the old system. Here's what it actually costs today, broken down into real ringgit figures.

## Why WhatsApp API Pricing Changed in 2026

Until 30 June 2025, Meta billed WhatsApp Business API by the **conversation** — a 24-hour window that covered unlimited messages once opened, regardless of how many templates you sent inside it. Since 1 July 2025, that model is gone. Meta now bills **per individual template message**, based on which of four categories it falls into: marketing, utility, authentication, or service. This is why older "conversation pricing" articles you'll find online are now out of date, and why your actual bill may look different from what a provider quoted you a year ago.

## Meta's Official Per-Message Rates for Malaysia

These are Meta's direct rates for messages sent to Malaysian phone numbers in 2026 — before any platform markup:

- **Marketing messages**: RM0.3467 per delivered message (promotions, broadcasts, announcements)
- **Utility messages**: RM0.0564 per message (order confirmations, delivery updates, appointment reminders)
- **Authentication messages**: RM0.0564 per message (OTPs, login verification codes)
- **Service messages**: Free and unlimited — any reply you send within 24 hours of a customer messaging you first costs nothing

The service-message window is the detail most SMEs miss: if your customers are messaging you directly to ask about products, order status, or support, those replies don't cost you anything at all. Costs only kick in when your business initiates contact using a marketing or utility template.

## Platform Fees on Top of Meta's Rate

Meta doesn't sell WhatsApp Business API directly to small businesses — you go through a BSP platform, and that's where most of the monthly cost actually comes from. Typical Malaysia-focused pricing tiers look like this:

- **Entry-level plans**: RM299–RM499 a month, covering one WhatsApp number, a shared inbox, and basic broadcast tools
- **Growth plans**: RM499–RM999 a month, adding chatbot flows, CRM integration, and multiple team-member seats
- **Pro/enterprise plans**: RM1,000+ a month for high-volume broadcasting, advanced automation, and multi-number management

Some international platforms charge in USD instead — expect roughly USD15 (~RM65) per month per connected number on top of Meta's message fees. Many providers also charge a one-off **setup/onboarding fee of RM500–RM2,000** to handle Meta Business verification and the green tick application, though a growing number of Malaysian providers now waive this.

## A Real Monthly Cost Example

Here's what an actual month looks like for a mid-sized Malaysian SME running a Growth-tier plan (RM499/month) with typical volume:

- 2,000 utility messages (order and delivery updates): 2,000 × RM0.0564 = **RM112.80**
- 500 marketing messages (monthly promo broadcast): 500 × RM0.3467 = **RM173.35**
- Platform fee: **RM499**
- **Total: approximately RM785/month**

An F&B business with fewer broadcasts but heavy customer-service traffic (mostly free service replies) could land closer to RM400/month on an entry-level plan, while a retail brand doing weekly promo blasts to a 10,000-contact list could see marketing-message costs alone climb past RM3,400 for that single broadcast — which is why segmenting your contact list before every broadcast matters as much as picking the right platform.

## Official BSP vs Reseller: What's the Difference

All WhatsApp Business API access runs through a Meta-approved BSP, but pricing varies depending on how that provider marks up Meta's base rate:

1. **Official/direct-rate providers** pass through Meta's per-message cost with a flat platform fee, no per-message markup
2. **Reseller platforms** may add 15%–25% on top of Meta's per-message rate in exchange for extra features like advanced chatbot builders or CRM integrations

Neither is automatically the wrong choice — a reseller markup can be worth it if their automation tools save your team hours of manual work. But always ask a potential provider to show Meta's base rate separately from their platform markup before signing, so you know exactly what you're paying for.

## API vs the Free WhatsApp Business App

If you're a solo operator or a very small team, the free WhatsApp Business App may still be enough — it supports one device, basic auto-replies, and a product catalogue at no cost. The API becomes worth paying for once you need **multiple team members in one inbox, automated flows, broadcast messaging to unlimited contacts, or CRM integration** — capabilities the free app simply doesn't offer. For a full breakdown of what automation and integration look like once you upgrade, see our guide on [WhatsApp Business API for Malaysian SMEs](/blog/whatsapp-business-api-malaysia-sme-automation-2026).

## How to Budget for WhatsApp API in 2026

1. Estimate your monthly message volume by category — count how many order confirmations, reminders, and promo broadcasts you actually send
2. Multiply utility/authentication volume by RM0.0564 and marketing volume by RM0.3467 to get your raw Meta cost
3. Add your chosen platform's monthly fee (RM299–RM999 for most SMEs)
4. Ask every shortlisted provider to itemise Meta's rate separately from their markup, in writing
5. Start with an entry-level plan and one number — you can upgrade once your broadcast volume justifies it

## Conclusion

WhatsApp Business API pricing in Malaysia isn't one flat number — it's Meta's per-message rate (RM0.0564–RM0.3467) plus a platform fee (RM299–RM999/month), and for most SMEs that totals RM600–RM1,500 a month once real messaging volume is factored in. faq.q: How much does WhatsApp Business API cost per message in Malaysia?
faq.a: Meta charges RM0.3467 per marketing message and RM0.0564 per utility or authentication message to Malaysian numbers. Service replies within 24 hours of a customer message are free and unlimited.

faq.q: What's the total monthly cost of WhatsApp Business API for a Malaysian SME?
faq.a: Most SMEs pay RM600–RM1,500 a month total, combining a platform fee (RM299–RM999) with per-message charges for a typical mix of a few thousand utility and marketing messages.

faq.q: Is there a setup fee for WhatsApp Business API in Malaysia?
faq.a: Many providers charge a one-off RM500–RM2,000 onboarding fee to handle Meta Business verification and the green tick application, though some Malaysian providers now waive this fee entirely.

faq.q: Are replies to customer messages on WhatsApp API free?
faq.a: Yes. Any reply sent within 24 hours of a customer messaging your business first counts as a free, unlimited service message — costs only apply to business-initiated marketing or utility templates.

faq.q: Should I use the free WhatsApp Business App instead of the paid API?
faq.a: The free app suits solo operators on one device. The paid API (from RM299/month) is worth it once you need multiple team seats, automated flows, or broadcasts to unlimited contacts.
